description: 4.12.5 + 23.4 - a nested `<program name= lang=>` with NO `use foreign:` in the parent. It is a FOREIGN LANGUAGE SIDECAR whether or not it also declares `port=`, so it emits no `new Worker(...)` and no worker bundle; pre-fix (S356) the 23.4 carve-out that suppressed the bogus worker keyed on `port=` ALONE, so this `port=`-less spelling of the same execution context was still compiled as a 4.12.4 web worker and shipped a 24-byte stub bundle. EXPECTATION CORRECTED S356 r3. This case previously asserted E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL ABSENT, on the reasoning that 23.4 already fails the sidecar closed at the `use foreign:name { ... }` site and two errors on one unbuilt shape is two diagnostics for one mistake. That reasoning holds only when there IS a `use foreign:` to fire at - and this case has none, so the carve-out was suppressing the ONLY diagnostic and the shape compiled to exit 0 with its body silently discarded. The carve-out is now CONDITIONAL: an UNCLAIMED sidecar is refused here, a CLAIMED one is refused by 23.4. Exactly one diagnostic per mistake either way - see the sibling case `foreign-sidecar-claimed` for the other half. Which CODES exist is unchanged; only the condition each one fires on was made precise. COVERAGE NOTE (S356 r3, correcting round 2's disclosure): `conformance/run.ts:203` checks `notCodes` UNCONDITIONALLY, so a `notCodes` entry genuinely bites even with an empty `codes` list. What the harness CANNOT check is artifact presence - nothing in the codes-only contract observes that no `new Worker(...)` reference and no `.worker.js` bundle were written. That half is covered by `compiler/tests/integration/nested-program-worker-artifact-emission.test.js` (the SIDECAR_APP fixture) and by `compiler/tests/integration/nested-program-execution-context-gate.test.js`.
rationale: §4.12.3's table gives "Foreign language sidecar | `name=`, `lang=` (non-WASM language) | Subprocess with HTTP/socket" — `port=` is a sidecar CONFIGURATION attribute (§4.12.2: "Port number for sidecar HTTP/socket communication"), not the discriminator. §4.12.3 normative (S356): the inline-worker context is selected if and only if `name=` is present and `lang=`/`mode=`/`route=`/`db=`/`port=` are all absent. The absence of a declaration-site diagnostic here is the deliberate carve-out recorded in the §34 row for E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL.
